published_statement: HPS p.8: 'From the numerical calculations, we see that for sufficiently large l, both the redshift and shape functions can be represented as a sum of two distinct components f(l) = F(l) + phi(l); r(l) = R(l) + rho(l), where F(l) and R(l) are strictly monotone increasing and phi(l) and rho(l) are bounded oscillating functions. ... We find that the oscillating modulation is composed of two modes with frequencies omega_1^2 = 1/(16K^2) and omega_2^2 = 1/(16K^2(4+3 ln F)), respectively, while in the limit of large l, R(l) ~ l and F(l) ~ (a ln l - b)^2 for a = 5.3 and b = 25.5. From these combined numeric and analytic calculations we see that for the chosen set of boundary conditions, R(l) -> l, thus our self-consistent wormhole connects two spatial regions which are asymptotically flat, modulo the Planck-scale wiggles. The redshift function however, does not approach a constant value as l -> infinity, so the metric as a whole is not asymptotically flat.'
published_hypotheses: H1 Static spherically symmetric metric ds^2 = -f dt^2 + dl^2 + r^2 dOmega^2 (eq. (2), p.4).

H2 Source: the Anderson-Hiscock-Samuel analytic approximation for a massless (m = 0), zero-temperature (kappa = 0) conformally coupled (xi = 1/6) scalar, with the renormalisation scale mu absorbed into f (eqs. (4)-(7), fn [20]); G = 8 pi <T> with K^2 = 1/(5760 pi).

H3 'for the chosen set of boundary conditions': eq. (9) throat data with the ONE displayed solution ln f(0) = -2/3 (p.7) -- the statement is about that solution, not the family -1 <= ln f(0) < 0 or the other solutions p.8 mentions (large throats with horizons; wormholes between bounded regions).

H4 The large-l form F ~ (a ln l - b)^2, a = 5.3, b = 25.5, is from 'combined numeric and analytic calculations' -- an asymptotic analysis 'taking into account and guided by the results of the numerical investigation' (p.7); the fitting range is not stated. The l -> infinity conclusion is therefore an extrapolation of a finite-range numerical solution through a fitted asymptotic form.
H5 'Asymptotically flat' is used in the sense that f approaches a constant (the spatial part is called asymptotically flat 'modulo the Planck-scale wiggles'); no formal definition is given.
H6 Whatever system HPS actually integrated (their printed eqs. (5)-(7) or a corrected one) -- HPS do not say; the tree records HPS_INTEGRATED_THE_PRINTED_SYSTEM = 'NOT DETERMINED' (hpscentre.py:279).

The failure does not depend on the definition chosen: f unbounded and a Komar integral that grows linearly (Part A3, B3) fail every definition that requires a normalisable static Killing field with finite mass at infinity -- named hypothesis: d/dt is the static Killing field (unique up to scale); not machine-checked.

A2 on the smooth part (r = l, f = F): G^t_t = 0 = G^th_th and G^l_l = 2a/(l^2 (a ln l - b)) exactly, conservation identity closes -- the smooth part needs a pure radial stress ~ 1/(l^2 ln l). A3 Komar integral M_K = r^2 f'/(2 sqrt f) = a l on the smooth part (diverges, and t -> lam t only rescales it), control Schwarzschild M_K = M. lacked_data: What HPS (1996-97) had: their own integration of eqs. (5)-(7) from eq. (9) data over an unstated range, and an asymptotic analysis guided by it. What came later or was not used: (i) the conservation test that exposes the three places where the HPS and Popov printings disagree and picks the one conserved reading (tree hpscentre.py:128-153; sibling gr-qc_9701064 audit) -- HPS may have integrated a non-conserved system (NOT DETERMINED); (ii) Popov 2003's statement that the AHS approximation is established for asymptotically flat spacetimes, which turns HPS's remark into a domain failure; (iii) long-range integrations (here to 1e5 K in both readings). EVIDENCE: having (i) and (iii) does NOT change the conclusion -- f grows without sign of saturation in BOTH readings (conserved <sqrt f> 6.0 -> 45.9, printed-M1 6.8 -> 36.5 over 300 -> 9.9e4 K; sibling ab-fit: local slope still rising at 8e4 K) and the Komar integral grows linearly in both; the fitted (a, b) move with the window (a 4.7-8.9) but the conclusion needs only a != 0. Having (ii) changes how the statement is USED (a domain hypothesis fails), not whether it holds. What could still move it: only behaviour beyond 1e5 K (the l -> infinity claim is an extrapolation for HPS and for this audit alike, hypothesis H4), and there is no evidence of saturation -- the local log-slope is increasing, not decreasing. M's hypothesis is therefore tested and NOT borne out for this result: the missing data (conserved system, longer range) confirm, and a later author (Hochberg-Visser 1998) states it more strongly.
grade_evidence: (1) READ: the tree's quotation (hpscentre.py:100) is verbatim HPS p.8 (hps_0.xml:1183-1185), and the owner line applies it to the same solution HPS state it for (eq. (9), ln f(0) = -2/3), naming the added support 'plus the measurement' -- no hypothesis dropped or weakened on the owner line; the only drift is the ledger summary's plural 'solutions' (wording). (2) Re-derivation agrees (sympy, exact): HPS's printed law diverges for every a != 0 and every normalisation of t, and its Komar integral grows as a l, against a finite control (Schwarzschild M_K = M). (3) Measurement agrees and is independent of the unresolved which-system question: both readings of the tree's system from eq. (9) data, integrated to 1e5 K, have strictly increasing <sqrt f> (>5x) and <M_K>/x flat within 3x (a finite mass would fall 330x). (4) No moved datum moves it: (a, b) are window-dependent fits, but only a != 0 matters and every window gives a > 4.6. Named limits carried with the grade: the l -> infinity claim is an extrapolation beyond 1e5 K (H4) -- the same limit HPS's own claim has; d/dt taken as the static Killing field; Popov's AF definition not re-read here. Recorded, not graded: HPS's smooth law is not self-consistent without the ripples (A4), and the spatial ripples are order one to 1e5 K, which is at odds with HPS's 'asymptotically flat, modulo the Planck-scale wiggles' for the spatial part and consistent with Hochberg-Visser 1998's 'no asymptotically flat spatial regions' -- a discrepancy between two printings, not a refutation.
what_would_change_the_grade: To NARROWED: a demonstration (analytic, or an integration well beyond 1e5 K) that the ripple-averaged source falls faster than 1/l^2 so that f saturates and the Komar integral converges on some reading or range of the eq. (9) data; or a reading of Popov's AF definition that the unbounded-f, linearly-growing-Komar metric nevertheless meets (not expected). To OPEN: evidence that the hps_0.xml text layer misstates p.8 (e.g. the PRL typesetting differs). To DATA-DEPENDENT: a window or reading in which the fitted a approaches 0. Nothing found here points that way.
